title: Suvarna Raj Wins Discus Gold as India Reach 15 Golds at Asian Para Games
excerpt: On day four in Aichi-Nagoya, Suvarna Raj's 15.66-metre throw won the women's F54 discus, Swati Chaudhary took archery silver and Manisha Ramadass and Pramod Bhagat took badminton bronze, moving India to 65 medals.
body:
• Suvarna Raj won the women's discus throw F54 gold on October 22 with 15.66 metres on her fifth attempt, giving India its 15th gold at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games.
  • Iran's Shahla Hadidi took silver at 15.45 metres and Vietnam's Nguyen Thi Ngoc Thuy bronze at 14.65 metres in the six-athlete final.
  • India added two more medals on the day in the ANI report: silver for para-archer Swati Chaudhary in the women's W1 individual event, and bronze for badminton pair Manisha Ramadass and Pramod Bhagat in mixed doubles SL3-SU5.
  • With those three medals, India's tally in the ANI report stood at 65 medals — 15 gold, 22 silver and 28 bronze — and fifth place in the Latestly medal table, up from 62 medals at the end of day three.

Suvarna Raj won India's first gold of day four at the Asian Para Games 2026, taking the women's discus throw F54 title in Aichi-Nagoya on Thursday, October 22, with a best effort of 15.66 metres, according to ANI reporting published by Latestly. It was India's 15th gold of the Games.

Competing in a six-athlete field, Suvarna recorded four throws beyond 15 metres across her six attempts. The winning throw came on her fifth attempt. Iran's Shahla Hadidi secured silver with 15.45 metres, while Vietnam's Nguyen Thi Ngoc Thuy claimed bronze with 14.65 metres.

Silver in Archery, Bronze in Badminton

Para-archer Swati Chaudhary won silver in the women's W1 individual event after losing the final to China's Mengkan Cen 4-6. Swati had led 4-2 after three ends and had a chance to win India's first archery gold of this edition, before Cen came back to take the final 6-4, ANI reported.

In badminton, Manisha Ramadass and Pramod Bhagat settled for bronze in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 event after losing their semifinal to Indonesia's Oktila Leani Ratri and Hikmat Ramdani. The Indian pair won the opening game but lost 21-16, 13-21, 17-21. Ratri and Ramdani now face India's Thulasimathi Murugesan and Nitesh Kumar in the final, which guarantees India at least a silver in that event and leaves a further gold in play.

"Competing in a six-athlete field, Suvarna recorded four throws beyond 15 metres across her six attempts."

Where the Tally Stands

At the end of day three India had 62 medals, with 14 gold. The three medals reported by ANI on Thursday took the tally to 65 medals — 15 gold, 22 silver and 28 bronze. The Latestly medal table for October 22 placed India fifth overall, behind China, Uzbekistan, Japan and South Korea, with China well clear at the top on 115 golds.

This is a day-update on a campaign already covered by The Videshi. It follows the October 21 results, when Nishad Kumar's double gold headlined a five-gold day for India, and it covers only what changed on October 22: a new gold in the field, a first archery medal of the day in silver, and a badminton bronze with another Indian pair already through to a final.

What Remains

The Aichi-Nagoya Games, the fifth Asian Para Games, opened on October 18 and conclude on October 24, according to Latestly's tally report, which put the event at about 2,590 to 3,000 athletes from 45 National Paralympic Committees across 18 para sports and 489 medal events, under the motto "Imagine One Heart," with the Nagoya City Mizuho Athletic Stadium as the main venue.

For India, the immediate watch is the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, where Murugesan and Kumar can convert a guaranteed silver into the contingent's 16th gold, and whether the fifth-place position in the table holds through the final two days against Iran and Thailand, who were level with India on 15 golds in the October 22 table.
